blocks.text: 6. Large Items May Need to Be Dismantled

c: Some objects cannot simply be carried through a doorway.
A large sofa may need to be maneuvered through a tight hallway.
A hot tub may need to be dismantled.
A large piece of furniture may need to be taken apart before removal.
If dismantling is required, ask the junk removal company about it before booking.
This helps ensure the crew arrives prepared for the actual job.

blocks.text: 7. The Job May Require More Than One Truckload

c: A property cleanout can involve far more junk than expected.
For example, an estate cleanout might include furniture, appliances, boxes, mattresses, clothing, electronics, and garage contents.
If everything cannot fit into one truck, the company may need to plan multiple loads.
That’s why photos and an accurate description of the job can be extremely helpful when requesting an estimate.

blocks.text: What Should You Tell a Junk Removal Company Before Booking?

c: The more information you provide, the easier it is for a company to determine whether it can accept your job.
Instead of saying:

b: “I have a lot of junk to remove.”

c: Try saying:

b: “I have two couches, a refrigerator, a mattress, several boxes, and garage junk. The items are located in the basement and garage, and the basement has stairs.”

c: This gives the company a much clearer picture.
You can also send photographs.

blocks.text: How Can You Make a Difficult Junk Removal Job Easier?

c: If you think your job may be challenging, there are a few simple things you can do.

items.title: Take Photos
text: Photographs help the company understand the size and type of items.

items.title: Make an Item List
text: Write down everything that needs to go.

items.title: Mention Heavy Items
text: Don’t surprise the crew with a piano, hot tub, or commercial appliance when they arrive.

items.title: Explain Access
text: Tell them about stairs, elevators, gates, narrow hallways, or parking restrictions.

items.title: Mention the Property Type
text: Let the company know whether it’s a house, condo, apartment, office, warehouse, or commercial property.

c: If you have electronics, appliances, renovation debris, or other unusual materials, ask whether they are accepted.
These simple steps can make the booking process much smoother.

text: Many full-service companies do. However, always confirm that the company accepts your specific item, especially if it is unusually large or heavy.
